app.setup.title_default.why: plain factual state, matches iOS/macOS on/off convention, distinct wording from the hedged failed-check title

app.setup.title_failed.s: 拡張機能の状態を確認できません
app.setup.title_failed.why: hedged verb 確認できません (cannot confirm) rather than asserting off, keeps it distinct from title_default

app.setup.detail_default.s: サイトを保護すると、意図しないクリックやタップを乗っ取られなくなります。
app.setup.detail_default.back: Once you protect a site, unintended clicks and taps can no longer be hijacked.
app.setup.detail_default.why: one plain declarative sentence carrying the whole value proposition, です・ます register

app.setup.detail_failed.s: Safariの確認がうまくいきませんでした。拡張機能をオンにすれば、このアプリが自動で気づきます。
app.setup.detail_failed.back: The check with Safari didn't go well. If you turn the extension on, this app will notice automatically.
app.setup.detail_failed.why: two clauses, no error code or jargon, second clause reassures with 自動で気づきます (notices automatically)

app.setup.open_button.why: verb+object button, generic enough to sit on both the setup screen and the welcome sheet verbatim

app.welcome.heading.why: the one place in the product allowed a warmer register; standard first-hello greeting formula

app.welcome.feature.invisible_layers.tit.why: concrete two-word noun phrase, not marketing language

app.welcome.feature.invisible_layers.det.s: 透明な層がページに重なり、押した場所とは違うものが反応します。
app.welcome.feature.invisible_layers.det.back: A transparent layer overlaps the page, and something different from where you pressed reacts.
app.welcome.feature.invisible_layers.det.why: describes what the person experiences, not the mechanism; term 透明な層 reused later for the overlay tag

app.welcome.feature.swapped_links.title.why: concrete noun naming the trick; すり替え reused later for the href-swap tag

app.welcome.feature.swapped_links.detail.s: 押してから離すまでの一瞬でリンクの行き先が変わり、思った場所に進めません。
app.welcome.feature.swapped_links.detail.back: In the instant between pressing and releasing, the link's destination changes, so it doesn't go where you thought.
app.welcome.feature.swapped_links.detail.why: concrete moment described with a natural て-chain rather than a fragment stack

app.welcome.feature.uninvited_windows.ti.why: short concrete noun phrase naming the trick

app.welcome.feature.uninvited_windows.de.s: 保護中は、押した場所が開くタブだけが開き、余計なものは紛れ込みません。
app.welcome.feature.uninvited_windows.de.back: While protected, only the tab for where you pressed opens, and nothing extra sneaks in.
app.welcome.feature.uninvited_windows.de.why: framed as a promise per the brief, not a description of the trick itself

app.welcome.feature.every_destination.ti.s: すべての移動先を記録
app.welcome.feature.every_destination.ti.why: names the rule-list feature concretely; 移動先 (destination) is the fixed vocabulary term used throughout

app.welcome.feature.every_destination.de.s: 見つかった移動先はすべて一覧に残り、このサイトだけか、すべてのサイトかを選んで許可・ブロックできます。
app.welcome.feature.every_destination.de.back: Every destination found stays in a list, and you can choose just this site or every site to allow or block.
app.welcome.feature.every_destination.de.why: concrete mechanism, uses the fixed 許可/ブロック verdict pair

app.welcome.feature.one_site_at_a_time.t.why: contrasts with automatic everywhere mode, concrete short phrase

app.welcome.feature.one_site_at_a_time.d.s: そのサイトを開いた状態でSafariのツールバーのUndirectボタンを押すと、そのサイトの保護がオンになります。
app.welcome.feature.one_site_at_a_time.d.back: With that site open, pressing the Undirect button in Safari's toolbar turns protection on for that site.
app.welcome.feature.one_site_at_a_time.d.why: names the toolbar button mechanism concretely per the vocabulary entry for toolbar button

app.nav.guarded_sites.why: matches the vocabulary term for guarded/watched site, short enough for a narrow sidebar column

app.nav.settings.why: Apple's own standard Japanese term for Settings, one word

app.nav.app_title.why: proper noun left untranslated, as the brief flags

app.rules.grouping.everywhere.why: short noun forming a clear contrast pair with サイト別 (by site)

app.rules.grouping.by_site.why: clear opposite of 全サイト

app.rules.empty_no_app.title.s: 拡張機能からの応答なし
app.rules.empty_no_app.title.back: No response from the extension yet
app.rules.empty_no_app.title.why: distinct wording (応答なし, no response) marks this as a wiring problem, not an empty-content state

app.rules.empty_no_app.detail.s: Safariで何かページを開くと、ここに表示されます。
app.rules.empty_no_app.detail.back: Open any page in Safari, and it will show up here.
app.rules.empty_no_app.detail.why: one short instruction, no setting to change implied

app.rules.empty_no_rules.title.why: terse two-word title, clearly distinct from the 応答なし wiring state above

app.rules.empty_no_rules.detail.s: 移動先を許可またはブロックすると、ここに表示されます。
app.rules.empty_no_rules.detail.back: Once you allow or block a destination, it shows up here.
app.rules.empty_no_rules.detail.why: explains the trigger for an entry appearing, plain

app.rules.footer.lifetime_count.s: これまでに%lld件の乗っ取りを阻止しました
app.rules.footer.lifetime_count.back: So far, has stopped %lld hijacking attempts
app.rules.footer.lifetime_count.why: Japanese has no plural inflection, so one form covers the ICU plural's 'other' category; %lld kept as the Swift placeholder, 阻止 (stop) is the fixed term for a blocked attempt

app.rules.row.state_blocked.why: 中 suffix marks the ongoing current state, pairs with 許可中

app.rules.row.state_allowed.why: clear opposite of ブロック中

app.rules.row.action_allow.why: verb form distinguishes this imperative menu action from the noun state 許可中

app.rules.row.action_block.why: verb form parallel to 許可する

app.rules.row.help_tooltip.s: この移動先を許可するかブロックするか選べます
app.rules.row.help_tooltip.back: Lets you choose whether to allow or block this destination
app.rules.row.help_tooltip.why: plain description of what the control does, Apple tooltip register

app.rules.row.use_default.why: names deletion of the explicit rule, distinct from the allow/block verbs

app.watched.empty.title.s: 保護中のサイトはありません
app.watched.empty.title.back: There are no sites being protected
app.watched.empty.title.why: mirrors the 保護中のサイト term used as the section's own label

app.watched.empty.detail.s: 困ったサイトを開いた状態で、Safariのツールバーにあるボタンを押すと保護が始まります。
app.watched.empty.detail.back: With the troublesome site open, pressing the button in Safari's toolbar starts protecting it.
app.watched.empty.detail.why: concrete instruction naming the toolbar button mechanism

app.watched.footer.s: サイトを増やすには、Safariのツールバーのボタンを使います。
app.watched.footer.back: To add a site, use the button in Safari's toolbar.
app.watched.footer.why: brief factual reminder that this screen cannot add a site itself

app.watched.row.guarded_badge.why: short state word matching the 保護中のサイト vocabulary

app.watched.row.stop_button.why: concise verb-noun matching Apple-style short trailing row buttons

app.watched.row.stop_tooltip.s: このサイトの保護をオフにします
app.watched.row.stop_tooltip.back: Turns protection off for this site
app.watched.row.stop_tooltip.why: plain tooltip description of the button's effect

app.settings.guard_toggle.why: single noun as the master toggle label; fixed term for the guard concept used across the app

app.settings.state_on.why: matches Apple's own katakana convention for switch states, generic across settings rows

app.settings.state_off.why: pairs with オン, matches platform convention

app.settings.mode_heading.why: concise heading introducing the where-the-guard-runs choice

app.settings.mode_watched.s: オンにしたサイトのみ
app.settings.mode_watched.why: user-centric phrasing per the brief, contrasts with すべてのサイト

app.settings.banner_toggle.why: names the in-page banner feature briefly, matches the note-in-the-page vocabulary term

app.settings.policy_heading.s: ルールのない移動先の扱い
app.settings.policy_heading.back: Handling of destinations with no rule
app.settings.policy_heading.why: concise heading using the fixed ルール/移動先 terms

ext.meta.description.s: ページが意図しないクリックを乗っ取り、別の場所へ開いたり移動させたりするのを防ぎます。
ext.meta.description.back: Prevents pages from hijacking unintended clicks and opening or moving you somewhere else.
ext.meta.description.why: slightly more explanatory register for a store-listing first impression, still plain verbs

ext.meta.app_title.why: brand fallback, same proper noun as elsewhere

ext.toolbar.tooltip_on.s: このサイトを保護中です
ext.toolbar.tooltip_on.why: plain state statement, です register held through the tooltip

ext.toolbar.tooltip_off.s: 押すとこのサイトを保護します
ext.toolbar.tooltip_off.why: doubles as the tooltip and the call to action per the brief, avoids a parenthetical off-state clause

ext.toolbar.tooltip_no_site.s: 保護できるページがありません
ext.toolbar.tooltip_no_site.why: brief explanation that there is nothing to guard on this tab

ext.popup.no_site_body.s: サイトを開いてから、このボタンを押してください。
ext.popup.no_site_body.back: Open a site, then press this button.
ext.popup.no_site_body.why: このボタン keeps the self-reference to the toolbar button rather than translating 'here' as a place

ext.popup.watch_switch_label.s: このサイトの保護を切り替える
ext.popup.watch_switch_label.why: accessibility label naming the switch's action plainly, for a row with no other visible label

ext.popup.watch_unknown.s: 保護できるページがありません
ext.popup.watch_unknown.why: same wording as the toolbar's no-site tooltip since the meaning is identical

ext.popup.watch_everywhere_mode.s: 設定で全サイトを保護しているため、この切り替えは使いません。
ext.popup.watch_everywhere_mode.back: Because Settings has all sites protected, you don't use this switch.
ext.popup.watch_everywhere_mode.why: names the setting-driven reason briefly with a ため clause

ext.popup.watch_master_off.s: 設定で保護がオフになっています
ext.popup.watch_master_off.back: Protection is turned off in Settings
ext.popup.watch_master_off.why: names the master-switch location, distinct from the per-site off wording

ext.popup.watch_on.s: このサイトを保護中です。オフにするとページが再読み込みされます。
ext.popup.watch_on.back: Protecting this site. Turning it off will reload the page.
ext.popup.watch_on.why: confirm-then-warn shape, mirrors watch_off as a before/after pair

ext.popup.watch_off.s: このサイトは未保護です。オンにするとページが再読み込みされます。
ext.popup.watch_off.back: This site is unprotected. Turning it on will reload the page.
ext.popup.watch_off.why: mirrors watch_on's sentence shape exactly, as the brief asks

ext.popup.page_heading.why: matches the fixed page/site vocabulary distinction, short heading

ext.popup.page_off.s: このページは保護されていないため、記録がありません
ext.popup.page_off.back: Because this page isn't protected, there's no record
ext.popup.page_off.why: dead key as of 2026-09-22 per the brief; written speculatively to match the voice of the other page-section states

ext.popup.page_quiet.s: このページでは何も起きていません
ext.popup.page_quiet.back: Nothing has happened on this page
ext.popup.page_quiet.why: plain short declarative for the quiet-page state

ext.popup.page_empty.s: 表示する項目はまだありません
ext.popup.page_empty.why: dead key per the brief; deliberate near-synonym of page_quiet rather than a distinct phrasing

ext.popup.stopped_one.why: Japanese has no singular/plural distinction, so this form is identical to stopped_other by design; 阻止 (stop) is the fixed term for a blocked attempt

ext.popup.stopped_other.why: identical to stopped_one; Japanese plural rule collapses both ICU forms into one string

ext.popup.seen_one.why: 記録 (record) kept distinct from 阻止 (stop) to preserve the seen-vs-stopped distinction from the vocabulary

ext.popup.tries_one.why: minimal counter fragment sized to sit among other terse comma-joined tags

ext.popup.recipe_heading.why: short label that reads naturally as a lead-in fragment before the colon-joined fix name

ext.state.blocked.why: compact noun form designed to combine with the scope fragments (see ext.scope.*), which carry their own leading separator

ext.state.allowed.why: pairs with ブロック as the compact opposite noun, same combination design

ext.state.removed.why: states a completed removal since this row has no destination to allow or block

ext.scope.here.why: code concatenates verdict then scope with no reordering possible; natural Japanese order would put scope first, so this is written as a trailing qualifier set off by a middle dot, a compact-badge convention, e.g. ブロック・このサイトのみ

ext.scope.everywhere.why: same trailing-qualifier design as ext.scope.here, for the forced verdict-then-scope concatenation

ext.scope.default.why: same design; 既定 matches the fixed default-policy term used elsewhere

ext.action.allow_here.why: standalone menu option string, not templated, so full natural Japanese word order is used directly

ext.action.allow_everywhere.s: すべてのサイトで許可

ext.action.block_here.s: このサイトでブロック
ext.action.block_here.why: parallel construction, completes the four-option set

ext.action.block_everywhere.s: すべてのサイトでブロック
ext.action.block_everywhere.why: parallel construction, completes the four-option set

ext.popup.policy_heading.s: ルールのない移動先の扱い
ext.popup.policy_heading.back: Handling of destinations with no rule
ext.popup.policy_heading.why: same wording as the app's settings equivalent for cross-surface consistency

ext.popup.bridge_warning.s: このページの設定により、保護の一部が動作していません。ページ側の制限によるもので、不具合ではありません。
ext.popup.bridge_warning.back: Because of this page's own settings, part of the protection isn't working. This is a limitation of the page, not a malfunction.
ext.popup.bridge_warning.why: two sentences, names it as the page's own limitation rather than a bug or a setting to fix, per the brief

ext.kind.click_catcher.why: terse tag reusing the 見えない罠 term family from the welcome screen

ext.kind.overlay.why: reuses the exact term from the welcome screen's invisible-layer detail sentence, avoids an unnecessary katakana loan (オーバーレイ)

ext.kind.synthetic_click.why: short plain tag for a script-dispatched click

ext.kind.window_open.why: established loanword with no common native alternative in this domain

ext.kind.form_submit.why: concrete short tag naming the mechanism

ext.kind.href_swap.s: リンク行き先のすり替え
ext.kind.href_swap.why: reuses すり替え from the welcome screen's swapped-links feature for consistency

ext.kind.back_hijack.why: reuses 乗っ取り (hijack) from the setup screen's payoff sentence

ext.kind.redirect.s: 同じタブでの強制移動
ext.kind.redirect.back: Forced move within the same tab
ext.kind.redirect.why: concrete tag for the core same-tab-redirect trick

ext.kind.pop_tab.s: 裏から開いた新規タブ
ext.kind.pop_tab.why: concrete tag naming the tab-under trick plainly

ext.kind.network_rule.why: names the strongest, earliest kind of block plainly

ext.reason.way_back.s: 元のサイトへ戻る経路があったため
ext.reason.way_back.back: Because it had a path back to the original site
ext.reason.way_back.why: concise ため-clause reason, matching the sibling reason strings' shape

ext.reason.sized.s: サイズを指定して開かれたため
ext.reason.sized.back: Because it opened at a specified size

ext.reason.took_press.s: 他の操作を奪ったため
ext.reason.took_press.why: extremely terse per the tight budget, same ため pattern as its siblings

ext.reason.default_allow.s: ルールがなかったため
ext.reason.default_allow.why: terse, uses the fixed ルール term, same ため pattern

ext.reason.own_code.s: サイト自身のコードによるため
ext.reason.own_code.back: Because it was by the site's own code
ext.reason.own_code.why: names the vouching mechanism briefly, same ため pattern as its siblings

ext.popup.rules_link.why: single term reused verbatim in the three spots the brief names

ext.popup.back_link.why: names where back returns to; matches the ext.popup.page_heading term for the same screen

ext.rules.empty.why: minimal single-row placeholder, terser than the app-side equivalent to fit the 1-2 word budget

ext.action.allow.why: single word; scope is already fixed by which section the row sits in

ext.action.clear.why: same wording as app.rules.row.use_default for cross-surface consistency

ext.popup.settings_heading.why: matches Apple's standard term, consistent with app.nav.settings

ext.settings.guard_label.why: same term as app.settings.guard_toggle for cross-surface consistency

ext.settings.guard_on.why: names the specific guard-running state, distinct from the generic オン used for other toggles

ext.settings.guard_off.why: pairs with 保護中 as the guard-specific opposite state

ext.settings.mode_heading.why: same wording as app.settings.mode_heading for consistency

ext.settings.mode_watched.s: オンにしたサイトのみ

ext.settings.banner_toggle.why: near-identical to app.settings.banner_toggle, shortened slightly to fit the tighter two-word budget

ext.action.report.why: verb+object action label per house UI-copy convention
